tasks.title: Companion UART load
tasks.statement: A companion receives LOCAL_POSITION_NED and ATTITUDE (28 bytes of payload each, MAVLink2 without a signature: +12 bytes of framing) at **{f} Hz** each. The FC port runs at **{b} baud** (8N1). What share of the link (in %) do these two streams take?
tasks.solution: Bytes on the wire = 2 · f · 40. An 8N1 UART uses 10 bits per byte, so the capacity = baud / 10 bytes/s (in the `SERIALn_BAUD` parameter these are the codes 57 … 921). Share = 2·f·40 / (baud/10) · 100%. The module's example: 50 Hz at 57600 → 69%, at 921600 → 4.3%. The course guideline is no higher than 50%.

tasks.title: How many targets in a row can be lost
tasks.statement: A companion sends a velocity target at **{f} Hz**, with `GUID_TIMEOUT = {t}` s. How many targets in a row can be lost on the link **with a margin**, so that the pause between received targets stays strictly below the timeout (the largest integer)?
tasks.solution: Targets go out with a period of 1/f; if k in a row are lost, the pause = (k + 1)/f. The condition with a margin: (k + 1)/f < t → k < f·t − 1; the largest integer is k = ⌈f·t⌉ − 2. When f·t is an integer, the boundary (k + 1)/f = t is exactly the timeout: the comparison in the code is strict, but a 400 Hz loop counting milliseconds and the link jitter make such a pause a lottery, so we do not allow it. 5 Hz and 3 s → 13 targets; 2 Hz and 1 s → 0: any loss comes right up to the timeout.
